sentence: 125	Pt, *********** *******, is a 17 y/o male[FP1] with tricuspid atresia with transposition of the great arteries and coarctation of the aorta[FP2], referred by ******** *******, ****, Transplant Coordinator, for Psychosocial Assessment for Heart Transplant Evaluation.

Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the patient, patient's mother, ****** *******, mother's fiancé, ******* ******, patient's grandmother, ****** *******, and review of the medical records.
SW spent approximately 60 minutes of face-to-face time with patient and family.
Living situation:  **, ***********, resides with his mother, mother's fiancé, and siblings[FP3] in *********, *******.
They **** a 4-bedroom home[FP4] with central a/c and heat.
They have city water[FP5].
Both adults smoke but there is no smoking in the home or in the car[FP6].

Demographics:  Mother:  ****** *******  ***:  **/**/****  Language: English   Education Level: 11th Grade[FP7]          Employment:  Unemployed[FP8]           Phone:  ***-***-****     Mom's Fiance:  ******* ******  ***:  **/**/****  Language: English   Education Level: High School Diploma[FP9]       Employment:  Unemployed[FP10]           Phone:  ***-***-****     Father: *********** *****  Prison in ********     Siblings in Home:  ******* ******* 28  ****** ****** 4     Siblings Not in Home:  ***** ******* 26 (*****)  ******** ******* 24 (*****)  ***** Mon 22 (New ****)  ******* ******** 13 (*******)     Other Children in Home (*******'s Children):  ****** ******* 8  ****** ****** 6  ****** ******* 4           Social History and Support Systems:  *********** lives with his mother, mother's fiancé (*******), two of his sisters, and three[FP11] ******* in *********, **.
They recently relocated from *** **** in ******* ** ****. ****** and ******* have been together for four years.
They are engaged with plans to be married[FP12].
They had to put plans on hold due to ***********'s illness but hope to be married this weekend while their family is all here.
They have a significant amount of family support present at the hospital at this time.
Their family has come in from ***** and New **** to be here.
[FP13] Maternal grandmother and grandfather are here from *** **** and plan to relocate to be near the family during this time[FP14].
This would be beneficial as grandmother has had custody[FP15] of *********** and been an advocate for his healthcare during the majority of his life per medical records from *** ****.
Per mom and grandmother, ***********'s father is in Prison in ******** for attempted to murder and is sentenced to life without the possibility of parole[FP16].
He has not had any involvement in ***********'s life and has not had any contact with the family since 2004.
Mom plans to be ***********'s primary caregiver post-transplant.
***********'s grandmother will be the secondary caregiver as she plans to relocate to ******* to be here for the family.
Neither are working at this time.   *********** is enrolled in the 11th grade special education program at ******* **** ******.
He has been diagnosed with a developmental delay[FP17].
He initially received PT and OT when he transferred to ******* **** but 'graduated' from the program.
He was sporadically under the care of a psychiatrist and psychologist[FP18] in *** **** by request of the Cardiologist in *** **** and had been diagnosed with ADHD and depression.
There was documented noncompliance with follow up and he had not received these services since move[FP19] to *******.
Family is not in agreement with the diagnosis or the medication treatment he received for the diagnosis.

They believe that he presents more as someone with bipolar disorder due to his frequent mood swings and family history of bipolar disorder (mom)[FP20]. *********** enjoys wrestling, video games, music, and dancing to ******* *******.
He is used to hospitalizations and ***** appropriately per grandmother's report.
He can become depressed during hospital stays but family being at bedside assists with improving his mood.
Mom denies any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc[FP21].
Course of illness:     *********** ******* is a 17 y/o male[FP22] with a history of tricuspid atresia with transposition of the great arteries and coarctation of the aorta[FP23].
He has been ********* with ***** and ****** procedures (initially fenestrated, now closed), mitral valve repair (**/****), pacemaker/AICD placement (2012).
Also with history of left CVA with resultant right-sided weakness s/p HIT induced coagulopathy, seizure disorder (last seizure */****), and small bowel resection following obstruction.
He is now admitted and currently being evaluated for a heart transplant.
Financial situation:  Both ****** and ******* are currently unemployed and not seeking employment at this time[FP24].
Just prior to the move to *******, mom was involved in an accident and is receiving a settlement from the accident.
The family is in section 8 housing and was just approved for food[FP25] ******. *********** also receives social security disability[FP26].
Mom is aware that the disability will be cut back if *********** is to remain in the hospital[FP27].   *********** is currently covered by New **** ********[FP28].
Mom reports that they have been approved for ******* Medicaid[FP29] but that she has been advised that she needs to pick one of the plans.
Once approved, this will cover all medical expenses at 100%.
Family has two vehicles and report that transportation will not be a barrier[FP30].
Family History:  Mom has a significant history of drug abuse[FP31].
She has been sober since 2007[FP32].
Due to the drug abuse she has been in and out of her children's lives. *********** has lived the majority of his life in his grandmother's care.
Mom has a significant mental health history and has been diagnosed with anxiety, bipolar disorder, and manic-depressive disorder.
She has had treatment in the past but is not currently undergoing care.
She has a very remote history of a suicide attempt and psychiatric hospitalization over 20 years ago.
She feels that her mental health has been stable during the past few years[FP33].
She also has a criminal record relating to the drug use but nothing since 2007[FP34][FP35].
There was no DCF involvement due to any of the above information as mom voluntarily placed her children with their grandmother[FP36].
However, mom did disclose that the father of her youngest child, ******, called in unfounded allegations because he was upset with her.
The case was closed and he no longer has any contact with the family.
Adherence:  There are significant concerns for adherence due to past records forwarded from patient's cardiologist[FP37] in *** ****.
There was documented history of noncompliance, specifically, when *********** was with his mother.
There was lack of follow through with psychology[FP38].
Upon move to *******, family was slow to seek physicians, medical care, insurance, resources, etc.
[FP39] SW discussed these concerns with family at length including the expectations of the transplant team.

Assessment and recommendations:  Mom was very ****** about her past but seems to be very committed to being there for *********** and her other children. ******* and grandmother are both here and also committed to being support for both mom and ***********.
They acknowledge that there has been noncompliance in the past[FP40] and that the transplant team has concerns due to that history.
They are willing to do whatever is necessary/requested including signing a contract of expectations.
There are concerns about their ability to maintain financially without *********'s social security disability income[FP41].
Family will need to come up with a plan to address this.
SW met with ******* alone to discuss his feelings regarding transplant.
He had a limited understanding of transplant but was able to verbalize to SW that his heart would have to be removed and someone else's put in.
He also stated that someone would have to die for him to live.
He went on to say that if someone had to die then he just 'wanted to pull the cord and be done'.
He was explaining it as such that the other person was being killed for him to live[FP42].
SW explored this further with him and explained different circumstances to his level of understanding.
He seemed to comprehend.
[MK43] SW allowed him to explore his feelings on his quality of life lived and life left to live and gave opportunity to openly discuss his wishes.
He would likely benefit from ongoing counseling to give opportunity to express his feelings on the topic and ask questions[FP44].
In the end, he verbalized that he would like to proceed with transplant.
